(7 March 2020 and onwards due to [[COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia]]){{cite web |title=وزارة الرياضة تُقرر تعليق الحضور الجماهيري في جميع المنافسات الرياضية في كافة الألعاب اعتباراً من يوم غدٍ السبت |url=https://www.spa.gov.sa/viewfullstory.php?lang=ar&newsid=2043837 |language=ar}} | attendance = 1,399,104 | average attendance = 8,479 | prevseason = [[2018–19 Saudi Pro League|2018–19]] | nextseason = [[2020–21 Saudi Pro League|2020–21]] | updated = 9 September 2020 }} The 2019–20 '''Saudi Pro League''' was the 45th edition of the [[Saudi Pro League|top-tier Saudi football league]], established in [[1974–75 Saudi Categorization League|1974]], and the 12th edition since it was rebranded as the '''Saudi Pro League''' in [[2008–09 Saudi Pro League|2008]]. The season started on 22 August 2019 and concluded on 9 September 2020.{{cite web |title=الإعلان رسميًا عن موعد انطلاق الدوري السعودي الموسم المقبل |date=18 May 2019 |url=https://www.eremnews.com/sports/football/arab/ksa/1817616 |access-date=6 June 2019 |archive-date=8 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200108192205/https://www.eremnews.com/sports/football/arab/ksa/1817616 |url-status=dead }} [[Al Nassr FC|Al-Nassr]] were the defending champions. The league was contested by the top 13 teams from the [[2018–19 Saudi Professional League|2018–19 season]] as well as [[Abha Club|Abha]], [[Damac FC|Damac]], and [[Al-Adalah FC|Al-Adalah]], who joined as the three promoted clubs from the [[2018–19 Prince Mohammad bin Salman League]]. They replace [[Ohod Club|Ohod]], [[Al Batin FC|Al-Batin]] and [[Al Qadsiah FC|Al-Qadsiah]] who were relegated to the [[2019–20 Prince Mohammad bin Salman League]].{{cite web |title=العدالة يرافق أبها وضمك إلى دوري المحترفين |url=https://arriyadiyah.com/645811 |access-date=6 June 2019}} On 7 March 2020, the [[General Sports Authority|Ministry of Sports]] announced that all matches would be played behind closed doors until further notice. On 14 March 2020, the Ministry suspended all sports competitions indefinitely due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.spa.gov.sa/viewstory.php?lang=ru&newsid=2047561|title=عام / وزارة الرياضة : تعليق النشاط الرياضي بالمملكة وإغلاق الصالات والمراكز الرياضية الخاصة|website=www.spa.gov.sa}} On 11 June 2020, the Ministry of Sports announced the resumption of sports activities with training starting on 21 June and games starting after 4 August 2020 and played behind closed doors.{{cite web| url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-saudi-sports/saudi-arabia-will-resume-sports-activities-without-fans-starting-from-june-21-idUSKBN23I3EQ| title=Saudi Arabia will resume sports activities, without fans starting from June 21| work=Reuters| date=11 June 2020}} On 1 July 2020, the schedule for the remaining matches was released. It was announced that the league would resume on 4 August 2020 and end on 9 September 2020.{{cite web |title=لجنة المسابقات برابطة #الدوري_السعودي_للمحترفين تعلن جدولة مواعيد الجولات المتبقية من |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210115154756/https://www.spl.com.sa/system/files/MBSLEAGUE_1.pdf |url-status=dead }} On 29 August 2020, [[Al Hilal SFC|Al-Hilal]] won the league for a record 16th time with two matches remaining, after defeating [[Al-Hazem F.C.|Al-Hazem]] 4–1.{{cite web |title=قبل النهاية بجولتَيْن.. الهلال يُتوَّج بلقب دوري كأس الأمير محمد بن سلمان |date=29 August 2020 (Riyadh)|Al-Shabab]].{{cite web |title=المرة الثانية.. الحزم يهبط |url=https://arriyadiyah.com/700875}} [[Al-Fayha FC|Al-Fayha]] were the third and final team to be relegated following a 1–0 defeat Sixteen teams will compete in the league – the top twelve teams from the previous season, the play-off winner and the three teams promoted from the [[2018–19 Prince Mohammad bin Salman League|MS League]]. '''Teams who were promoted to the Pro League''' The first team to be promoted was [[Abha Club|Abha]], following their 2–2 draw away to [[Al-Nojoom FC|Al-Nojoom]] on 30 April 2019. Abha will play in the top flight of Saudi football after a ten-year absence.{{cite web |title=أبها يعود إلى دوري المحترفين بعد غياب 10 أعوام |date=30 April 2019 |url=https://www.alwatan.com.sa/article/1007843/%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%A7%D8%B6%D8%A9/%D8%B3%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%AF%D9%8A%D8%A9/%D8%A3%D8%A8%D9%87%D8%A7-%D9%8A%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%AF-%D8%A5%D9%84%D9%89-%D8%AF%D9%88%D8%B1%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%85%D8%AD%D8%AA%D8%B1%D9%81%D9%8A%D9%86-%D8%A8%D8%B9%D8%AF-%D8%BA%D9%8A%D8%A7%D8%A8-10-%D8%A3%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%85}} Despite losing to [[Al-Qaisumah FC|Al-Qaisumah]], they were crowned champions on 11 May 2019 due to Damac's 1–1 draw with [[Al-Ain FC (Saudi football club)|Al-Ain]].{{cite web |title=أبها بطلا لدوري The third and final team to be promoted was [[Al-Adalah F.C.|Al-Adalah]], who were promoted on the final matchday following their 2–0 win at home against Damac on 15 May 2019.{{cite web |title=العدالة يكمل عقد المتأهلين إلى دوري المحترفين |date=15 May 2019 |url=https://sabq.org/97wqsJ}} Al-Adalah will play in the top flight of Saudi football for the first time in history. '''Teams who were relegated to the MS League''' The first team to be relegated was [[Ohod Club|Ohod]], ending a 2-year stay in the Pro League following a 3–1 home defeat to [[Al-Fayha FC|Al-Fayha]] on 12 April 2019.{{cite web |title=الفيحاء يعلن هبوط احد رسمياً والتعاون يتغلب على القادسية |url=https://freeswcc.com/ar/archives/214812 |access-date=2019-06-07 |archive-date=2020-01-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200102150325/https://freeswcc.com/ar/archives/214812 |url-status=usurped }} The second team to be relegated was [[Al-Batin F.C.|Al-Batin]], ending a 3-year stay in the Pro League following a 1–0 home defeat to an already relegated Ohod side on 11 May 2019.{{cite web |title=الباطن يهبط إلى دوري الدرجة الأولى السعودي |url=https://www.goal.com/ar-sa/%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1/%D8%B1%D8%B3%D9%85%D9%8A%D8%A7-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B7%D9%86-%D9%8A%D9%87%D8%A8%D8%B7-%D8%A5%D9%84%D9%89-%D8%AF%D9%88%D8%B1%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AF%D8%B1%D8%AC%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D9%88%D9%84%D9%89-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B3%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%AF%D9%8A/1uhblub1zur2n1ufiy89jtkuck}} The third and final team to be relegated was [[Al-Qadsiah FC|Al-Qadsiah]], who were relegated on the final matchday following a 2–2 home draw with [[Al-Hazem F.C.|Al-Hazem]].
